So if you don't feel like reading feel free to skip it. Some time ago I really wanted to start making games of my own. I've been a life long gamer and it seems such an awesome thing. So I started to learn on my own and managed to make a game and release it, then another, and then anther. Sure, at the start they were crap but I sat down for months and years and managed to start and finish a project. And now I'm working on my forth game and I've been getting so much positive feedback. The demo currently holds 100% positive review rating and playtesters are saying very nice things. I continue to work every day to make sure I complete it. It's a moral dilemma sim / trolley problem style game based on The Milgram Experiment. As always I use no AI to make it. item.title: GovBrief Today #601
item.description: Police in Springfield, Missouri, handcuffed a woman at Monday night's city council meeting and ticketed her for a disturbance, listing the evidence as "middle finger to mayor." She came to speak against the city's 41 Flock license plate cameras, but the council had just voted to shelve a review of them and cancel public comment on the subject. She raised it anyway, during comment on a housing bill. Her microphone went dead, and she kept speaking with both middle fingers in the air until police led her out. Two days later, a prosecutor in Indianapolis charged five current and former police officers with using their department's Flock cameras to track exes and spouses. One, an 18-year veteran, is charged with stalking women he met around town, including one from his workout class. The department caught them by checking who ran each search and why, the kind of review Springfield's council wouldn't let its residents talk about.
